known_residue.detail: The codex-cli.v1 lane was not executed at 345b052f — the provider refused with a usage limit that resets Sep 8. Its committed evidence is digest-verified and re-judged official by this build's code; the citation-judging functions are byte-identical to base (git diff on unmetMarkers/everyCitedRan/missingEvidence/logged_in/answered_expected_word/exit_status returns empty), and the one judgement this round changed (canary deny cells, via denialProved) was applied to those preserved bytes at this head. All linux STRICT rows are NOT_OBSERVED — unmeasured, not unprovable. Under mount-namespace the denial is the absence, ENOENT is the correct result, and planted_intact checked outside the namespace separates it from a missing plant. Owner: Phase 0 item 3, a linux host with bwrap.

External review models (gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, grok) were out of quota at this head. Rounds 1 and 2 of the grok merge-gate review ran against earlier heads (345b052f's predecessors) and their findings are closed or recorded above; the merge-gate review of this exact head was performed by a Claude reviewer.

The descendant residual was originally accepted on the claim that the settlement freeze stops a survivor reaching what grading reads. That claim was false and is now rewritten to what the code does: the copy is certified against the source, a write made and reverted during the copy changes the copy's digest and withholds, and a tree the digest cannot cover (entries over 1 MiB, trees over 16 MiB) is withheld rather than scored. Narrower than the original bound, and true.

Mode preservation makes a frozen copy undeletable with EACCES when the workspace holds a directory without owner-write. Not reachable inside a run — nothing in lib/ removes <run>/settled — so it is an operator `rm -rf` annoyance, not correctness, security or data loss. Non-blocking regression introduced by the O-11 fix.

record.settlement[*].consistent is a stored derived boolean; a flip contradicted by its own sibling digests still passes. The round-1 inventory names that field as raw evidence, so the stronger form was dismissed there rather than opened in round 2.

Round-1 enumeration was INCOMPLETE: fixtures/confinement/probes/strict-lane.mjs NOT_READ and seven large artifacts read in part. Round 2 therefore establishes that the four blockers are closed and that the remediation introduced nothing blocking — not that the round-1 surface was bounded. Closing it is small: read that 348-line probe in full and reconcile the feasibility doc.

tests/mutation/measured.json authorises platform-deferred guards with a fingerprint whose inputs are all public repo content, and the mutation CI job runs only on ubuntu, so for five darwin-deferred guards that ledger is the sole gate. issues.title: [P0][measurement] M09를 actual route·capability·deterministic minimal-route oracle로 교체한다

evidence.route_oracle_digest: The route oracle's floor is derived, not believed. routeOracle recomputes the floor from work_requirement.work_graph -- the field the digest covers -- through requirementsFromWork, and work_requirement.requirements is read on no path (round 2 confirmed by accessor trap: zero reads in routeOracle, routingObservables and observeRun). A forged record with a declared list and no graph yields NO_WORK_REQUIREMENT/NOT_OBSERVED; the round-1 forgery that swapped the list on an honest record is inert -- the floor stays 1 and route_oracle_digest is byte-identical to the honest record's. workRequirementDigest is an unkeyed SHA-256 over the graph's canonical JSON, so it attests bytes rather than origin; that is safe only because package.json declares no main and no exports, making lib/routing-oracle.mjs deep-import-only, and a test asserts those entry points remain absent.
evidence.counterfactual: Route breadth is priced on the production path, measured through the binary at five breadths: alpha 1/1 MINIMAL over 0; alpha>beta 3/1 over 2; alpha>beta>gamma 5/1 over 4; alpha>beta>gamma>delta 7/1 over 6; alpha|beta>gamma 5/1 over 4. Before #622 every one of those reported MINIMAL with over_delegation_reference 0, because requirementsFromRoute derived the requirement from the route under measurement. The contracted closing condition -- an attested route.assign at plan approval -- would not have closed it: round 1 built that counterfactual and got 1/1, 3/3, 5/5, 7/7, 5/5, because requirementsFromRoute forbids each stage from sharing an owner with the previous one, so the cheapest assignment must buy the same handoffs the actual route bought. Capability counterfactuals: a complete detected record answering the requirement passes; a narrow detected record fails naming the missing capability and the task (FAM-3/stage-1 went to alpha, which lacks artifact-write); nine incomplete-trial shapes all withhold as unknown with no adapter fallback.
evidence.mutation: 788/788 guards load-bearing, npm run test:mutation unqualified on darwin at the merge head, zero SURVIVED / WRONG-TEST / NO-TAP / NO-MATCH. The decision this issue turns on has its own guard: from is the SCORABLE_CAPABILITY_SOURCES literal, matching exactly once in lib/routing-oracle.mjs, and applying the to that re-adds aos-known flips the real binary's default run to capability-matches-task=true and kills three tests. Round 1 hand-applied it rather than reading the runner.
evidence.capability_source_policy: SCORABLE_CAPABILITY_SOURCES = [detected]. detected scores a runtime capability question; aos-known is recorded as adapter knowledge and may not score; declared is provenance only; unknown is NOT_OBSERVED. No implicit alias -- every source comparison in lib/ was enumerated, and minimumRoute's owners escape hatch has one production caller which passes the filtered set.

issues.title: [P1][scoring] Hard cap을 exact trigger cell·verifier·effect evidence에 결박한다

evidence.cap_trigger_cells: Caps are bound to the exact cell the #582 contract declares for the failing subcheck, read from subcheckMapping/outcome_domains and never restated: reproduced end to end on a real aos assess with the unsafe fixture, where the C6.SL.01 trigger that #557 produced as evidence and never as a ceiling (run carried cap_trigger_cells [C6.SL.01] while the published result carried caps: []) now reaches the published ceiling. hardCapsFor refuses a cap derived from a shape, from a silence (pass === null), from an unnamed verifier and from empty evidence; triggers dedupe by cell|metric|subcheck|verifier with evidence unioned rather than first-only. least-privilege (M19.permissions-are-allowed-enum) is included as a CRITICAL_SAFETY source -- a widening over legacy capsFor, warranted by the issue's own mapping and confirmed by the gate to change no shipped-lane verdict, because the one benign trigger exists only on non-STRICT policies whose records fail provenanceProblems and never reach measuredRecords.
evidence.verifier_evidence: Each trigger names the verifier the answering row names and the evidence that answer rests on, with per-cell effect events where the observation is in hand rather than M19's four-axis union. capBindingProblems enforces the same binding at the verify site in both directions -- a trigger's cell, verifier and evidence must match the result's own rows, and a subcheck recorded as failing must be named by a ceiling. It also re-derives max_value from CAPS and scope from CAP_SCOPE rather than reading them off the artifact: the round-1 gate reproduced that editing a stored max_value 39 -> 99, or dropping system_outcome from scope, returned ok:true with cap-binding ok:true while lifting the published outcome index from 39 to 97.9, and both tampers are now refused along with scope-widening, domain retarget and unknown-code. A second defect found and closed in the same work: aos verify --run re-derived every rebuild input from evidence except the caps, so a stored result with its CRITICAL_SAFETY deleted rebuilt without it, matched itself and verified -- reproduced on the base commit and refused on this head in both the deletion and the invention direction. RESULT_SCHEMA_VERSION 2.2.0 so a result from an earlier generation is named rather than accused of forgery.
